subject: history
topicDisplay: Changes in Health and Medicine in Britain, c.500-present
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Medieval medicine was largely based on the Theory of the Four Humours, developed by:
questions.explain: The humoral theory of the ancient Greeks/Romans dominated medieval medicine.

questions.q: During the Black Death (1348), many people believed disease was caused by:
questions.explain: Without germ theory, people blamed miasma, God or the alignment of planets.

questions.q: The medieval Church slowed medical progress by:
options: Discouraging dissection and challenging new ideas
questions.explain: The Church promoted Galen's ideas and limited human dissection.

questions.q: Andreas Vesalius made major advances in:
questions.explain: Vesalius corrected Galen's anatomical errors through careful dissection.

questions.q: William Harvey is famous for discovering:
questions.explain: Harvey (1628) showed the heart pumps blood around the body in a circuit.

questions.q: Edward Jenner developed the first vaccine (1796) against:
questions.explain: Jenner used cowpox to protect against smallpox, founding vaccination.

questions.q: Louis Pasteur's germ theory (1861) was important because it showed that:
questions.explain: Germ theory replaced miasma theory and enabled targeted prevention and treatment.

questions.q: John Snow demonstrated in 1854 that cholera was spread by:
questions.explain: Snow linked cholera cases to a water pump, supporting public-health reform.

questions.q: Joseph Lister introduced ___ to reduce infection in surgery.
questions.explain: Lister's antiseptic methods dramatically cut surgical infections.

questions.q: Florence Nightingale improved health outcomes mainly by:
options: Improving hospital hygiene and nursing standards
questions.explain: Nightingale's emphasis on cleanliness reduced hospital death rates.

questions.q: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin, the first antibiotic, in:
questions.explain: Fleming observed penicillin mould killing bacteria; it was later developed as a drug.

questions.q: The National Health Service (NHS) was established in:
questions.explain: The NHS provided healthcare free at the point of use for all.

questions.q: A key factor speeding up medical progress in the 19th century was:
options: Scientific advances such as the microscope and germ theory
questions.explain: Better science and technology enabled the identification of pathogens.

questions.q: Anaesthetics such as chloroform (James Simpson) allowed surgeons to:
options: Perform longer, more complex, pain-free operations
questions.explain: Anaesthetics removed pain, though infection remained a problem until antiseptics.

questions.q: The discovery of germ theory was a turning point because it:
options: Explained the true cause of disease, enabling vaccines and antiseptics
questions.explain: Understanding germs underpinned modern prevention, hygiene and treatment.

questions.q: Government Public Health Acts (e.g. 1875) improved health by:
options: Providing clean water, sewers and better housing
questions.explain: State action on sanitation cut deaths from infectious disease.
